- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion speed — if price is near 30-day moving average, forecast should be slightly below average for 2–3 days before reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict late-period (last 10–15 days) values; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for days 25–30.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as baseline for correction.
